i0: These **paired conjunctions** join two words, phrases or clauses: *I speak **both** English **and** Persian. We can go **either** today **or** tomorrow.*
i1: For *both, either* and *neither* on their own (*both of them, either day*), see [Quantifiers](/blog/grammar/quantifiers/#qn-both-either-neither).
ben-both-and.s: ***Both X and Y*** = X and Y, the two together: *Both my mother and my father are teachers.* With two subjects, use a **plural** verb.
ben-both-and.b1: ***Both… and*** adds emphasis: the two things are true: *She speaks **both** French **and** Spanish.*
ben-both-and.b2: Two subjects with *both… and* take a **plural** verb: ***Both** Ali **and** Sara **are** coming.*
ben-both-and.b3: Put *both* directly before the first item: *She's **both** clever **and** funny.*
ben-either-or.t: Either… or: one or the other
ben-either-or.s: ***Either X or Y*** = X or Y, one of the two: *We can either take the bus or walk.* In negatives, ***not… either… or*** = not X and not Y. With two subjects, the verb agrees with the **nearest** one.
ben-either-or.b0.2.1: *I **don't** speak **either** French **or** German.* (= I speak neither)
ben-either-or.b0.3.1: *Either Ali or **his sisters are** coming. Either his sisters or **Ali is** coming.*
ben-either-or.b1: With two subjects, the verb agrees with the **nearest** subject: *Either my parents or **my brother is** going to pick you up.*
ben-either-or.b2: Use *either… or* for a choice between **two** things. With more items, *or* alone is usual: *You can pay by cash, card **or** cheque.*
ben-neither-nor.t: Neither… nor: not one and not the other
ben-neither-nor.s: ***Neither X nor Y*** = not X and not Y: *Neither my brother nor my sister can swim.* Use a **positive** verb, because *neither… nor* is already negative.
ben-neither-nor.b1: Use a **positive** verb: *I **have** neither time nor money.* (= I don't have time or money), not *I don't have neither…*
ben-neither-nor.b2: With two subjects, the verb agrees with the **nearest** subject: *Neither the teacher nor **the students were** ready.*
ben-neither-nor.b3: *Neither… nor* is a little formal. In conversation, *not… either… or* is common: *I **don't** like **either** coffee **or** tea.*
x.ben-both-and-b04: *Both* goes directly before the first item.
q.ben-neither-nor-b04: Which sentence means the same as *I don't like football or basketball*?
